title: Book One · Chapter 9: Three Coins
story:
Ronan has three coins in a small cloth bag.

He takes them out after dinner. He puts them in a line on the table board. Two are small. One is larger and darker.

"Can I buy a bike with these?" he asks.

Dad is wiping his tools. He stops with the cloth in one hand.

"No," he says.

"A small bike?"

"Not yet."

Ronan pushes the big coin closer to Dad.

"This is a big one."

"I see. But even a used bike costs much more."

Mum sits down with a shirt across her knees. A button hangs by one thread.

"We can ask about prices one day," she says. "You can write the price in your book. Then you can save for that bike."

"When?"

"We can look in a shop another day. Tonight we will stay home."

Ronan puts the coins back in the bag. They make a small heavy sound together. He likes that sound, but it is not a bicycle sound.

He looks around for a box. His old paper box is in the kitchen. It holds towels now. He takes one towel out and looks inside.

"That box has a job," Mum says.

"I gave it to you."

"You did."

Ronan puts the towel back. Dad looks under the bed and brings out an empty tea box. The lid has a blue flower on it.

"Mrs Lan gave us this box to use. Do you want it?"

Ronan opens it. It smells like leaves. There is one dry bit in a corner.

He takes that out. He rubs the inside with his clean cloth. Then he drops the three coins in.

The sound is bigger now.

Mum finds a piece of paper. She draws three small circles. Ronan puts a number beside each circle, slowly. The last number faces the wrong way. He rubs it out and tries again.

"Do I get a coin every day?" he asks.

"No," Mum says. "Some days there won't be any spare money. These three still stay yours."

"And my school pencils?"

"We buy school things," Dad says. "Mum and I will pay for your school pencils. Keep your own coins in your box."

Ronan closes the lid. He moves the box under the shelf. Then he moves it to the end of his bed.

"Can I earn more?"

"Maybe," Mum says. "We can choose a small job together. But we do not pay you to eat dinner. You put your own shoes away too. That is not a paid job."

Ronan looks at his shoes. One is under her chair. He pulls it out with his foot.

"What about putting Dad's shoes away?"

"Look at those big shoes!" Mum says. "That is a very large job."

Dad lifts one foot toward her. She moves the shirt out of reach and laughs.

Ronan puts both his shoes by the door. Then he takes the tea box to Dad.

"Please ask me first. Then you can use this money."

"I will not take your money," Dad says.

He does not put a hand on the lid. Ronan holds the box himself.

Before bed, he counts the coins once more. Three is still three. He puts the paper under them. Then he closes the lid. He leaves it beside his bed. He wants to save for a bike. Dad knows that now. Mum knows it, too.
studyGuide:
## 先看情节提示也可以

Ronan想攒钱买自行车；他用旧茶盒保存自己的三枚硬币。

## 从认词到读句子

1. **Ronan / has / three coins in a small cloth bag.** Ronan／有／三枚硬币，装在小布袋里。
2. **He / puts the paper / under them.** 他／把纸放下／放在它们下面；them指三枚硬币。

---

重点表达：save＝积攒；coins＝硬币；costs＝需要花费；spare＝多余的。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 为什么把硬币拿到桌上？
2. Mum 和 Dad 怎样帮助他保留自己的计划？
